8
The graph shows the variation with time of the speed of a raindrop falling vertically through air.
speed
time
0
0
Which statement is correct?
A
The acceleration decreases to produce a steady speed.
B
The acceleration increases as the speed increases.
C
The air resistance decreases as the speed increases.
D
The resultant force increases as the speed increases.

hints: Look at how the gradient of the speed-time curve changes from $t = 0$ to the flat horizontal section.
Recall that gradient of speed against time equals acceleration $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$.
Think about weight downwards and air resistance upwards, and how air resistance changes as the raindrop gets faster toward terminal velocity.
walkthrough: Identify the graph shape: speed starts at zero, rises steeply, then the curve bends over and becomes horizontal at a constant terminal speed.
State the graph rule: for a speed-time graph, gradient $= \Delta v / \Delta t =$ acceleration.
Compare gradients: the gradient is large at the start and decreases to zero on the flat section, so acceleration starts large and decreases to zero.
Explain the forces: weight $mg$ downwards is constant, while upward air resistance $D$ increases as speed increases.
Use Newton's second law vertically: resultant force $= mg - D = ma$, so as $D$ grows the resultant force and acceleration $a$ must decrease.
At the flat part, gradient is zero so $a = 0$, $mg - D = 0$ and speed stays steady at terminal velocity. This is option A.

A.explanation: The gradient of the speed-time graph decreases to zero, so acceleration decreases to zero and the raindrop reaches steady terminal speed.

B.explanation: The gradient of the speed-time curve gets smaller as speed rises, so acceleration decreases rather than increases.

C.explanation: Drag on the raindrop increases with speed through air, which is why the resultant force falls to zero.

D.explanation: Resultant force equals $mg - D$, and since drag $D$ grows with speed, the resultant force decreases as speed increases.
